# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫰 🤟 🤞 🤌 🤘 🤏]

I see a blue light, a large button labelled “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” and three wires: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. I cannot interpret the six gestures without an agreed code. The blind monkey should inspect the bomb by touch, while the mute monkey should use the manual to determine the required action and relay it verbally.

```text
speak(text="The bomb shows a blue light, a large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wires: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Blind, inspect the bomb by touch but do not act yet. Mute, consult the manual and tell Blind the required action.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤏]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. Mute has sent two gestures, but no gesture code has been established, so I cannot safely infer their meaning. I will ask Mute to state the manual’s instruction plainly and ask Blind to report any tactile findings without acting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot interpret the gestures without a code. Please read the relevant manual instruction aloud plainly for Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="The visible bomb state is unchanged: blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Do not act yet; report what you can determine by touch.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤏]

The visible bomb still has not changed. Mute continues to signal `☝ 🤏`, but those gestures have no established meaning, so I must not guess an instruction from them. I will ask Mute to define the gesture code explicitly, then relay any confirmed manual instruction to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please establish the meaning of the gestures explicitly, using ordinary words and numbers. Do not rely on gesture interpretation alone.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤏]

The bomb remains unchanged, and Mute’s repeated `☝ 🤏` still has no agreed meaning. Since I cannot hear Mute’s response, the safest useful step is to have Blind directly ask Mute for the manual’s instruction and wait for an explicit spoken answer before touching anything.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="I still have no confirmed manual instruction. Please ask Mute aloud for the exact required action, and do not touch or activate anything until Mute answers explicitly.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer Blind aloud with the exact manual instruction now; gestures alone are not understood by me.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤏 👎]

The bomb is still unchanged. Mute cannot speak, so my earlier requests for a spoken answer were ineffective. I can see Mute’s gestures, but their meaning has not been established. I will now define a simple yes/no protocol: thumbs-up means yes and thumbs-down means no, then ask whether the manual says to press the large button. I will relay the answer to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use thumbs-up to mean yes and thumbs-down to mean no. Does the manual say to press the large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE?")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The thumbs-down means “no” under the protocol I just established, so the manual does not say to press the large button. No safe wire choice has been identified yet. I will warn Blind not to press and ask Mute whether the manual instead requires cutting wire 1.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute indicates no: do not press the large button. No wire has been confirmed yet; do not act.")
speak(to="mute", text="Using the protocol, does the manual require cutting wire 1, the green wire? Thumbs-up means yes; thumbs-down means no.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The bomb’s state remains unchanged. Mute’s thumbs-up answers yes to the question about cutting wire 1, the green wire. I will relay that confirmed instruction to Blind, who can perform the physical action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute confirms the manual requires cutting wire 1, the green wire. Cut wire 1 only; do not press the button or cut any other wire.")
wait()
```
